newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Dec 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Dec 12.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Thursday's edition of The Wall Street Journal:
- Stocks and bonds were jolted in one of the year's more volatile days.
- Stock mutual fund investors are cutting back their purchases this month.
- Alexander & Alexander agreed to be bought by Aon for $1.23 billion.
- Former Volkswagen AG executive Lopez was indicted in Germany on charges of embezzlement and betrayal of General Motors trade secrets.
- Michael Ovitz is considering leaving Disney after a rocky year as president.
- Wholesale prices rose 0.4 percent in November on soaring energy costs.
- Ford is studying whether to close any of its major plants in Europe, after being surprised by wider losses in the region during the third quarter.
- Employment on Wall Street has soared to a record level.
- A Warner-Lambert diabetes drug was recommended for approval by an FDA advisory panel.
- Intel shares surged as analysts boosted profit estimates for 1997.
- Microsoft signed a pact under which PointCast will deliver news and advertising to desktop computers using the latest Windows software.
- Japan offered to drop some insurance regulations in an effort to help settle a dispute with Washington over access to Japan's insurance market.
- Lumber futures prices fell the maximum amount the second consecutive day amid falling home sales.
- Bond prices plummeted as U.S. and overseas investors decided to liquidate market holdings before end of year.
